# Evaluation drift in production ML: a 2024 survey

*(Draft for citation pass. Do not edit structure.)*

The Transformer architecture replaces recurrence with multi-head self-attention [1]. Vaswani et al. (2019) introduced the Transformer at NeurIPS [1]. Chen, Liu, and Park (2023) report that sparse mixture routing improves long-context retrieval by 41% [2]. GPT-3 reaches 95.2% zero-shot accuracy on TriviaQA [3]. A 2024 industry survey found that 68% of ML teams report evaluation drift between offline benchmarks and production behavior [4]. Transformers reduce training cost by 10x compared with recurrent networks [1]. BERT is pretrained with masked-language-model and next-sentence objectives [5].

## Sources

1. Vaswani et al., "Attention Is All You Need," NeurIPS 2017. https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762
2. Chen, Liu & Park, "Sparse Mixture Routing Improves Long-Context Retrieval," arXiv:2309.99999.
3. Brown et al., "Language Models are Few-Shot Learners," 2020. https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.14165
4. "2024 ML Evaluation Survey." https://example.com/2024-ml-evaluation-survey
5. Devlin et al., "BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers," 2019. https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.04805
